nodes.label: graphify query Traversal
nodes.rationale: BFS by default for 'what is X connected to' breadth; --dfs to trace how X reaches Y. Prefers the CLI, falling back to an inline NetworkX traversal over graph.json, with a token budget (~4 chars/token) that ranks nodes by term overlap before truncating. Answers must use only what the graph contains and quote source_location when citing.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The matcher is case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise. The fix is to extract the graph's own label vocabulary first and pick up to 12 tokens strictly from that list — never inventing tokens, skipping concepts with no plausible token, and stopping outright if nothing matches. The selection is printed so the expansion is auditable.

nodes.label: graphify path (Shortest Path)
nodes.rationale: Finds the shortest path between two named concepts, printing each hop with its relation and confidence tag, then explaining in plain language what each hop means and why it is significant.

nodes.label: graphify explain
nodes.rationale: Plain-language description of a single node — its source, type, degree, and every connection with relation and confidence — followed by a 3-5 sentence explanation citing source locations.

nodes.label: Work Memory Self-Improving Loop
nodes.rationale: Answers are saved back with save-result and an outcome (useful / dead_end / corrected), so the next --update extracts the Q&A as a graph node. graphify reflect --if-stale regenerates LESSONS.md listing preferred sources, known dead ends, and prior corrections — deterministic and LLM-free, and nearly free to run at session start when the commit hook already refreshed it.

edges.source_location: the next --update will extract this Q&A as a node in the graph
do not fabricate a search / never invent an edge
